prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: advisory only; no autonomous dispatch/control; command authority retained; segmentation/time-sync/health-checks/audit-logging required. Participants: local fire agencies/county emergency management/state wildland fire resources/aviation support units/cooperating public safety partners. North Lookout Camera Mast sends Thermal Spot Snippet/bearings; South Lookout Camera Mast supplies triangulation/Camera Cleaning Log. Smoke Classifier Module supplies smoke/growth/confidence/Ridge Shadow Mask; cannot solely justify aircraft commitment. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern) fuses reconnaissance/camera/weather projections, down-weights degradation, produces traceable detections/perimeters/recommendations/probability bands. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle) supplies terrain-weighted weather/Wind Shift Bulletin. Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): triage. Duty Detection Officer (Orion): evidence/decision verification. Confirmation requires persistent smoke/thermal plus independent corroboration or authorized judgment; uncertainty stays triaged; dismissals searchable. Confirmed Ignition State permits planning, not uncleared dispatch. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): charging/positioning/launch/recovery/shelter; must report readiness/health/recovery before task release; maintenance controller produces Battery Swap Ticket. Drone Tasking Service defines missions/windows/images/altitudes/abort criteria. Drone Pilot Operator verifies endurance/return/field-route/suppression-aircraft separation. Imagery requires weather/airspace/communications clearance, orthorectification/grid-registration; verifies access/spread/structure exposure before crew assignment. Air Attack Supervisor (Redtail) reviews location/confidence/airspace before reconnaissance/retardant authorization; Wind Shift Bulletin informs sequencing/holding/drop approaches; Airspace Restricted State requires route/altitude acceptance. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold) tracks availability/target-time/turnaround/priority; blocks release for incomplete approvals/airspace/readiness; produces Runway Release Note after runway validation. Tanker Base Manager matches Retardant Batch Slip to aircraft/quantity, resolves loading discrepancies. East Retardant Loading Pump produces metered/sealed slip; both it and West Retardant Loading Pump report state/flow/outages. Loading status is not approval; supervisor commitment required. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): identity-preserving approved-instruction fallback; impairment requires Orion alternate-contact verification. County Emergency Liaison receives confidence/threats/civil-coordination. Maps

New part:
S146: The Crewline Mobile Tablet shows approved suppression objectives, aircraft caution areas, and current assignment notes for crews operating near the incident.
S147: The Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges nearby aircraft activity before personnel are moved into a drop zone or a reconnaissance overflight area.
S148: The Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console sends the Suppression Drop Receipt after a completed drop has been recorded and checked for required timing fields.
S149: During extended attack, the Caldera Incident Command Portal preserves each aviation decision with the approving supervisor, operational period, and reason for change.
S150: The County Emergency Liaison can view approved aviation status and public safety implications without gaining authority to alter dispatch or suppression records.
S151: If reconnaissance, loading status, or weather guidance conflicts with an active plan, the system holds the affected recommendation for Air Attack Supervisor review before further action.
S152: This section describes how helitack and ground crews receive assignments, staging information, hazards, and updated intelligence from the support system during active wildfire operations.
S153: When a held recommendation is cleared, the Air Attack Supervisor selects the operational intent in the Caldera Incident Command Portal.
S154: The Caldera Incident Command Portal records each assignment package with an objective, time validity, confirmation status, and required acknowledgments.
S155: The Crewline Mobile Tablet displays the current division assignment, route guidance, rally location, and assigned communications channel for the logged-in crew.
S156: The Helitack Crew Leader receives the same operational package with aviation constraints and landing zone notes after Air Attack Supervisor approval.
S157: Ground crew assignments are formatted for field execution and avoid analytic scores that are not needed for tactical movement.
S158: Staging information is maintained as georeferenced areas and route descriptions so that crews can confirm location without relying on informal landmarks.
S159: The Crewline Mobile Tablet caches the latest accepted staging information and marks any expired package as unavailable for execution.
S160: If the Confirmed Ignition State changes the perimeter or priority area, the Caldera Incident Command Portal marks affected crew assignments for review before release.
S161: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine updates hazard summaries when fire spread estimates, access constraints, or field observations change.
S162: The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine applies the Ridge Shadow Mask when estimating crew-visible fire edge confidence in steep terrain.
S163: The Smoke Classifier Module uses the Camera Cleaning Log to suppress confidence changes caused by lens contamination and service timing.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
